newsitem.title: CANADA: Chretien says Canada heading for elections.
newsitem.headline: Chretien says Canada heading for elections.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien said on Wednesday he intended to call federal elections but did not say when he would do so.
"We will go to the people of Canada, and because of the good government that they have, we have now the lowest interest rates in Canada in 35 years," he told the House of Commons.
Most government officials and political analysts expect Chretien to issue the call this weekend, probably on Sunday, for elections on June 2.
He and his Liberal Party were elected with a solid majority in October 1993 and he does not have to go to the polls until October 1998.

Opposition Reform Party leader Preston Manning charged that Chretien was going early because he had run out of ideas, but the prime minister said Canada had gained respect during his term and the economy had strengthened.
